content.title: Everything that happened in the 2026 WNBA Draft
content.text: Follow live reaction as the 2026 WNBA Draft welcomed a new class of rookies into the leagueFormer UConn star Azzi Fudd was drafted No. 1 overall by the Dallas Wings. Getty ImagesFudd taken first overall, UCLA sets draft recordThe Dallas Wings selected Azzi Fudd with the No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 WNBA Draft.Fudd is reuniting with former UConn teammate and last year’s first selection, Paige Bueckers. The Minnesota Lynx selected another guard, TCU's Olivia Miles, with the No. 2 pick. Former UCLA teammates Lauren Betts, Gabriela Jaquez and Kiki Rice went to the Washington Mystics, Chicago Sky and expansion Toronto Tempo at picks No. 4-6 respectively, days after winning a national championship. They were part of five Bruins taken in the first round and six overall, both WNBA Draft records for a single collegiate program.The Golden State Valkyries took LSU star Flau'jae Johnson at No. 8 and subsequently traded her to the Seattle Storm, while the Indiana Fever selected Raven Johnson at No. 10, reuniting her with former South Carolina teammate Aliyah Boston — and former college rival Caitlin Clark.Share your views: live@theathletic.comSKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementNo Offseason breaks down WNBA DraftWant instant analysis on all the picks and stories from tonight’s WNBA Draft?Well then join The Athletic “No Offseason” livestream where our Zena Keita, Sabreena Merchant and Chantel Jennings break down tonight’s results.Onward to the WNBA regular season Getty ImagesWith the WNBA Draft in the rearview, it’s time to look ahead to the regular season.Preseason basketball starts on April 25 with four games. The regular season tips off on May 8 with three games. The Connecticut Sun take on the New York Liberty. The Toronto Tempo plays its inaugural regular season game at home against the Washington Mystics.The Golden State Valkyries and Seattle Storm square off in the nightcap.On May 9, the defending champion Las Vegas Aces battle the Phoenix Mercury. Caitlin Clark and the Indiana Fever face No. 1 pick Azzi Fudd and the Dallas Wings. It’s going to be a fascinating season in professional women’s basketball. Get ready, hoops fans! Valkyries GM declines comment on Johnson tradeA somewhat stunning answer from Golden State Valkyries general manager Ohemaa Nyanin regarding the Valkyries’ decision to trade No. 8 overall pick Flau'jae Johnson for No. 16 overall pick Marta Suárez and a future second-rounder from the Seattle Storm, hat-tip Nathan Canilao of the Bay Area News Group:💬 “I don't have a lot of details to share, one because I am exhausted. Two because I want to be very thoughtful when I'm talking about the humans and their basketball abilities and how they would or would not show up for our squad.”Johnson excited to join Fever Getty Images Raven Johnson on joining the Indiana Fever:💬 “You’re talking about a team that could possibly win the championship. … They have a lot of vets that I can learn from and they're winners. … So to go to a program like that, that has the same mentality as me of winning, is phenomenal.”Johnson, Clark set to join forces Getty Images There is plenty of familiarity between Caitlin Clark and her new teammate in the Indiana Fever backcourt, Raven Johnson.During Iowa’s Final Four win over South Carolina in 2023, Clark famously waved off Johnson when she was open at the 3-point line late in the game. Johnson was a redshirt freshman then shooting just 24.1 percent from 3-point range. The incident briefly went viral but did not appear to linger, and got overshadowed by Clark’s tension with LSU’s Angel Reese in the national championship game days later.Johnson got her revenge a year later, though, when South Carolina faced Iowa in the national championship. In Clark’s final collegiate game, the all-time leading scorer in NCAA Division I basketball history was held to just 10-for-28 from the field as South Carolina dominated Iowa to win the title — with Johnson as Clark’s primary defender.The version of Johnson that now teams up with Clark (and former South Carolina teammate Aliyah Boston) in Indiana is a much more complete player, however. Johnson’s shooting and playmaking dramatically improved throughout her college career, and she shot 39.8 percent from 3-point range this past season.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementLiberty favorites to win WNBA title Getty ImagesPer BetMGM, the New York Liberty are the favorites to win the WNBA title. Their futures odds come in at +225. The Las Vegas Aces have the second-best odds at +350.The Indiana Fever, with Caitlin Clark, have the third-best odds at +375. Portland Fire inaugural draft class Getty ImagesAnd here is the first-ever draft class for the WNBA’s other new franchise, the Portland Fire:Iyana Martín Carrión (7th overall)Frieda Bühner (14th overall)Taylor Bigby (31st overall)Bigby and a 2027 third-round pick have been traded to Connecticut in exchange for Serah Williams, per my colleague Sabreena Merchant’s reporting below.Toronto Tempo inaugural draft class Getty ImagesThe inaugural draft class is complete for the Toronto Tempo. Solid four draft picks to kick off their first ever season as a franchise.Kiki Rice (6th), Teonni Key (22nd), Saffron Shiels (26th) and Charlise Dunn (36th) were selected. Here is Tempo general manager Monica Wright Rogers on the draft class.💬: “Tonight was about continuing to build with intention.“We are focused on identifying players who fit the style of play we want to establish, who bring competitiveness and versatility, and who are excited by the opportunity to help build something new.”South Carolina players drafted Getty ImagesSouth Carolina advanced to the women’s college basketball national championship a week ago.A week later, several names were called onto the stage at the WNBA Draft. Below were the South Carolina players selected. Two of them drafted in the first round: Raven Johnson (Indiana Fever)Madina Okot (Atlanta Dream)Ta'Niya Latson (Los Angeles Sparks)Draft highlight: Flau'jae Johnson dealt from Valkyries to Storm Getty Images When the Golden State Valkyries selected Flau'jae Johnson with the eighth overall pick, our Chantel Jennings thought the choice was a great fit for the expansion franchise that had just made the playoffs in its first year of existence.Apparently, the Valkyries did not agree.Minutes later, Golden State sent Johnson, one of the best players in LSU women’s basketball history, to Seattle in exchange for 16th overall pick Marta Suárez and a future second-round pick from the Storm.Easily the biggest trade of the night, and one which could reverberate for many years to come.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementUConn players drafted Getty ImagesUCLA rightfully deserves a lot of attention for its record-setting number of draftees taken tonight in the WNBA Draft. For the UConn Huskies, who lost just once last year in the women’s Final Four to South Carolina, they only had two players get drafted.Sure, one of them is the top of the draft in Azzi Fudd. Nothing to be upset about.The other was Serah Williams who will stay in the state of Connecticut and play for the Sun. Draft highlight: Fudd goes first overall to Dallas Getty Images Unlike the past several years, there was legitimate intrigue as to who would go No. 1 overall in this WNBA Draft. The Dallas Wings, picking first for the second straight year in a row, decided to go with continuity. Azzi Fudd, the former UConn star, will rejoin her former Huskies teammate and last year’s first overall pick Paige Bueckers in Dallas. The two will join with veteran Arike Ogunbowale to form a formidable backcourt trio as the Wings attempt to return to the playoffs for the first time since 2023.Flau'jae in new hatYour browser does not support the video tag.Because Flau'jae Johnson was traded from Golden State to Seattle, she needed to change hats.This is Johnson with an updated Storm hat. TRADE: Fire deal Bigby to SunThe Portland Fire are trading Taylor Bigby and a 2027 third-round pick to the Connecticut Sun for Serah Williams, a team source confirms to The Athletic. ESPN first reported the swap of the two players who were just selected in the third round tonight.Bruins make history with 6 selections Getty Images Through the first three picks of the WNBA Draft's first round, the defending national champion UCLA Bruins did not hear any of their seniors' names called.That changed quickly once pick No. 4 came, and the run on Bruins did not stop.The Washington Mystics selected Lauren Betts, the Most Outstanding Player of this year's NCAA Tournament, with the fourth pick. The Chicago Sky followed it up by picking Gabriela Jaquez at No. 5, and the Toronto Tempo made it three consecutive UCLA selections by taking Kiki Rice with No. 6.After Mystics took another Bruin at No. 9, Angela Dugalić, and the Connecticut Sun took Gianna Kneepkins with the final pick of the first round, UCLA made history as the first program to place five players in the draft's first round.That wasn't all. Charlisse Leger-Walker's selection in the second round made UCLA the first program with six draft picks in a single year.It's been an April to remember for the UCLA Bruins, and the celebration certainly continued today.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementBest players to not get drafted Getty Images There were lots of talented players who did not get drafted tonight in the WNBA Draft.Yarden Garzon is one of them. The Maryland senior guard was named to the all Big Ten third team this past season, averaging 12.5 points per game on 40.5 percent shooting from the floor. Raegan Beers, who became a staple in the women’s NCAA Tournament, also didn’t get selected tonight. She averaged 15.8 points per game in her senior season at Oklahoma. Kyla Oldacre, who scored 11 points in the women’s Final Four for Texas, went undrafted tonight. Mystics with haul of picks Getty Images The Washington Mystics had six (yes six) picks tonight in the WNBA Draft.Below were their selections:Lauren BettsAngela DugalićCotie McMahonCassandre ProsperDarianna Littlepage-BoggsRori HarmonFull third round resultsBelow are the full third-round results in the WNBA Draft:Zee Spearman (Wings)Tonie Morgan (Sky)Serah Williams (Sun)Rori Harmon (Mystics)Amelia Hassett (Sparks)Charlise Dunn (Tempo)Taylor Bigby (Fire)Kokoro Tanaka (Valkyries)Grace VanSlooten (Storm)Jessica Timmons (Fever)Manuela Puoch (Liberty)Eszter Ratkai (Mercury)Kejia Ran (Dream)Jordan Obi (Aces)Lani White (Lynx)Lani White closes out draftThe Minnesota Lynx, with the final pick in the draft, select Lani White out of Utah.The 2026 WNBA Draft is over.
